title: Element distinctness requires at least N log log N full-B2 gates at every sufficiently large length

claims.statement: Joint CircuitBreaker theorem under rules.md: the following declaration defines ONE fixed eligible total uniform NP family in the pinned full B2 model at actual input length n. Its full guarantee and its declared projection both hold unconditionally, for all sufficiently large integer lengths with the quantifiers specified by the theorem kinds. Both score source claims assert this ENTIRE declaration, not separate lemmas. Let L(n)=c*n^p*(log2 n)^q*(log2 log2 n)^r with the exact parameters in guarantee.leading. Let R(n) be the sum of the monomials in guarantee.remainder.terms, each coefficient times n^exponent*(log2 n)^log_exponent*(log2 log2 n)^loglog_exponent; an empty sum is zero. There exists N such that C_B2(f_n)>=L(n)-R(n) for every integer n>=N. All remainder coefficients are the exact declared constants. Declaration: {"convention":"uniform-np-full-b2-actual-length-all-lengths-v1","family":"One fixed total language L with slices on all bit lengths N. If N<4 reject. Otherwise choose the largest integer w>=1 with n_w=2*w*2^w<=N, partition the first n_w bits into 2^w consecutive records of 2w bits, and accept iff these records are pairwise distinct; ignore the remaining N-n_w bits. A fixed deterministic polynomial-time pairwise-comparison evaluator decides L. Its NP verifier accepts exactly the empty witness when this evaluator accepts, with witness bound zero.","guarantee":{"kind":"eventual_lower_bound","leading":{"coefficient":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"1"},"exponent":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"1"},"kind":"polynomial_log","log_exponent":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"0"},"loglog_exponent":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"1"}},"remainder":{"kind":"explicit","terms":[]}},"projection":{"exponent":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"1"},"kind":"lane_endpoint"},"theorem":"For this fixed language L in P, the minimum full-B2 gate count satisfies C_B2(L_N)>=N*log2(log2 N) at every sufficiently large integer input length N, with coefficient one and empty remainder. Consequently for each real A>0 we have C_B2(L_N)>=A*N at every sufficiently large integer N. These are corollaries of Theorem 2.2 of OpenAI, The matrix multiplication exponent is nine fourths (November 24, 2026), over F_2 on one list. The proof transfers the theorem to unrestricted nonuniform circuits and pads to all lengths while preserving an Omega(N*(log2 N)^sigma) bound for a fixed existential sigma>0.","version":"circuitbreaker-expression-v2"}
